summary_paragraph: A woman with ESRD on hemodialysis via a right tunneled femoral catheter, HIV/AIDS on HAART with opportunistic infection prophylaxis, and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on chronic warfarin (subtherapeutic INR) was admitted for persistent sharp right groin/thigh pain and thigh swelling near her new dialysis catheter shortly after a recent hospitalization for MRSA catheter-associated bacteremia. Evaluation showed no local signs of catheter infection and bilateral lower-extremity ultrasound was negative for DVT; symptoms were felt most consistent with local irritation/scar tissue, managed with scheduled acetaminophen and PRN oral hydromorphone. She remained without systemic infectious symptoms; a blood culture drawn during admission had no growth at discharge, and she continued vancomycin dosed with hemodialysis per Infectious Disease/OPAT plan. Headache with transient blurry vision resolved without intervention. Chronic hypotension was managed with continuation of midodrine. She was discharged back to extended care with plans for ongoing dialysis/vancomycin, continuation of HIV and renal medications, and outpatient warfarin dose adjustment with repeat INR later in the week.
problems: End stage renal disease on hemodialysis
HIV/AIDS on HAART with opportunistic infection prophylaxis
Recent MRSA bacteremia on vancomycin with hemodialysis
Subtherapeutic INR/abnormal coagulation profile on long-term warfarin for atrial fibrillation and catheter thrombosis risk
Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications (history)
